claims.text:
23. permutation-importance

Target / packet: ai-permutation-importance · D1. Prerequisites: ai:correlated-coefficients.

Nearest / distinct payoff: correlated-coefficients → ai-correlated-coefficients. Unstable coefficients are distinct from loss change after permuting one correlated feature versus the group in a fixed predictor.

Finite primary model: Held-out columns x_1=x_2=[0,1,2], target y=[0,1,2], fixed predictor (x_1+x_2)/2 gives MSE0. Reverse x_1 alone: predictions[1,1,1], MSE2/3. Reverse both columns together: predictions[2,1,0], MSE8/3.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: An alternate fixed predictor using x_2 alone ignores x_1, so permuting x_1 has no loss effect, while group reversal still gives MSE8/3. Importance depends on the fitted model, evaluation data and perturbation. It is not a causal contribution.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict which perturbation hurts more. On recall, change the predictor to x_2 alone and explain why the unused correlated column now has zero importance.

Required observable evidence: Show actual permuted rows, predictions and held-out loss. Group permutation preserves within-group pairing. Keep columns distinct from row coordinates.

Source obligation: [Maintainer permutation-importance documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/permutation_importance.html), acquired §5.2 and §5.2.3 correlated-feature discussion. Exact grouped reversal and losses are local constructions, not an empirical estimate.
 Shipped local model and displayed expression addresses: model.ts compute; Demo.tsx Figure; Stage retained computed witnesses.
